bc_bulletheads_south.blurb: Bulletheads South is a cluster of smaller crags at the Bulletheads end of the Stawamus Chief above Squamish, strung together by ledges rather than offering the long multi-pitch lines found at the neighbouring central section. Twenty routes mix trad and bolted lines, with most of the grades sitting between 5.10 and 5.11 and a handful of easier climbs at 5.8 and 5.9. The faces catch a blend of morning shade and afternoon sun, and the upper lines look out over Howe Sound. Reach it by a short forested walk on the Chief trail. Late spring through early autumn suits it best.

bc_rock_lady.blurb: Rock Lady is a large, bus-sized boulder beside a creek in Squamish's Paradise Valley, sitting low in the valley at roughly 200 ft. Twenty problems cover a very wide spread, from the easiest grades up to V10, though most fall in the V2 to V5 range. The climbing is vertical and technical, built on crimps and small holds, and the setting under the trees is attractive, with sunlight filtering through in the afternoon. It is a good stop for someone who likes precise face climbing rather than roofs and powerful moves.

bc_the_dihedrals.blurb: The Dihedrals is a section of the Stawamus Chief above Squamish, sitting on the darker middle of the big dome's face. It is almost entirely traditional climbing: of twenty routes, eighteen are trad, with one aid line and one bolted line. Routes run from three pitches to well over ten, so expect long days on a big granodiorite wall rather than quick laps. The grades lean hard, mostly 5.11 to 5.13, with only a couple of easier lines in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. Cracks, corners, roofs and ledges make the character varied. It suits experienced parties with a full rack.

bc_kootenay_crag.blurb: Kootenay Crag is a compact cliff at Nelson in the West Kootenays, known as the town's place for steep, demanding climbing, in contrast to the easy slabs at other local crags. The routes are short but steep, mostly bolted with a good number of trad lines and a couple of multi-pitch outings. Of twenty routes, most are sport. Grades cluster around 5.11, with several in the 5.12 and 5.13 range and few easy options, so it is a project crag more than a beginner stop. A single 60 m rope covers everything.

bc_the_terraces.blurb: The Terraces is a popular wall in the Grand Canyon section of Skaha Bluffs near Penticton in the Okanagan, reached by a trail that drops down the side of the canyon. Most of its twenty routes are bolted, with a few trad lines, and the grades run from 5.8 up to 5.12, with the bulk around 5.10 and 5.11. It makes a sensible warm-up spot for the harder walls further along the canyon, though it is not especially beginner-oriented. Spring and fall are the comfortable seasons; summer gets very hot, so start early. Expect company on good days.

bc_nicklen_wall.blurb: Nicklen Wall is a small section of the Aberdeen Columns, a basalt crag in the hills southeast of Vernon in the Okanagan. The columns here are known for clean cracks, and this wall follows suit with nearly all trad lines plus one aid route. Climbs are gentle by trad standards: a few easy fifth-class lines at the bottom end and most of the rest at 5.9 and 5.10, so it suits climbers building experience on natural gear. The wall sits at roughly 1,350 m; a lone fir above the right-hand boulder field is the landmark to aim for. Bring bug spray.

bc_bear_skull_boulders.blurb: Bear Skull Boulders is the main cluster in the Bear Skull sector of the Hunter Creek bouldering area near Hope in the Fraser Valley, set in forest beside the neighbouring Warm Up sector. There are twenty problems, spread widely: many in the V0 to V3 range, a good run of V4 to V6, and a single harder outlier. The climbing is technical, with careful footwork on gritty, textured rock, and some tops are awkward, so bring two or more pads. Spring through fall is the best window for dry, cool conditions. The grades are generally considered honest.

ca_pit_west_side_the.blurb: The Pit is a grotto-like corner on the back of Indian Rock, a small rhyolite outcrop in a Berkeley hillside park. It holds twenty-nine problems, nearly all bouldering with a couple of top-rope lines. Most are easy to moderate, with plenty from V0 to V4, a handful of harder ones around V7, and a few that go well beyond. The slightly overhanging rock is mostly smooth, and the shape of the problems favours technique over height. This is a sociable, inner-city spot, busiest after work and on weekends, and a crash pad helps. The shade holds much of the day.

_conflicts.bc_bulletheads_south: One page (https://app.advcollective.com/climbing/chasse-right-at-the-bulletheads-south-in-squamish) calls the rock limestone, contradicting the stored granodiorite (the same page also mentions granite walls); stored value kept. Thin evidence overall: only one page is specifically about Bulletheads South.
_conflicts.bc_the_terraces: Parking: stored parking name says Smythe Road upper lot, while one search result said all access is via the Braeside lot at the end of Valleyview Road; not fetched, nothing written.
